method: Every one of the 17 sources was fetched fresh with curl -sL -A "public-water-quality-pipeline/0.1 (checker)" into a private scratchpad folder (CMR endpoints kept as raw compact JSON; HTML pages kept raw and also stripped of tags with sed then HTML-entity-decoded with python3 html.unescape; the release notes were read from the researcher-supplied local .txt extraction). A Python script normalized runs of whitespace to a single space in both each claim's quote and the corresponding source text and tested literal substring containment for all 100 claims, without altering any non-ASCII character. The 3 mechanical misses and all 97 mechanical hits were then reviewed by hand against surrounding context to judge whether the quote actually supports the claim's value/note (not just whether it exists), including a byte-level check of two curly-vs-straight punctuation mismatches, a check of the raw HTML/JSON href attributes for the shapefile links, the CyAN File Search Launch link and the TEA HTTPS distribution prefix, and manual confirmation of every page-number and JSON-field locator against the fetched sources.

not_found_review.topic: A cells-per-mL conversion relation (e.g. a multiplier applied to CIcyano to yield cells/mL) in the V6 release notes
not_found_review.finding: Confirmed absent. The word 'cells' does not appear anywhere in the release notes text at all (a case-insensitive grep of the full local .txt file returns zero hits). The release notes give only the DN-to-CIcyano formula (CIcyano = 10**(DN * 0.011714 - 4.1870866)); the cells/mL range (~10,000 to 7,000,000 cells/ml) is stated only on the NASA Earthdata project page, with no formula or citation connecting CIcyano to a cell count.

discrepancy_review.note: Confirmed in fresh fetches: release notes say 2017-present (src-release-notes-v6); CMR collection time_start is 2016-04-25T00:00:00.000Z (src-cmr-collection-olci); the Earthdata landing page says 'Temporal Extent 2016-04-25 to Present' (src-earthdata-collection-olci); the Earthdata project page says Sentinel-3A OLCI '2016-present' (src-earthdata-project-cyan); the EPA page says 'publicly available from 2016 to current day' (src-epa-cyan); and the OB.DAAC file-search page labels the weekly period 'Weekly [2007-Present]' (src-obdaac-cyan-file-search-api). All six quotes verified present as stated.

Confirmed: release notes state SRTM 60-meter data provided the land mask (src-release-notes-v6, PAGE 4); the Earthdata project page states a 50m land mask for CONUS and 500m for Alaska (src-earthdata-project-cyan). Both quotes verified present as stated; genuine unresolved conflict.

Confirmed: the Earthdata landing page's Data-at-a-Glance panel and the UMM-C FileDistributionInformation both say netCDF-4, while the actual granule returned by CMR is a .tif and the release notes describe 8-bit GeoTIFF. All four quotes verified present as stated.

Confirmed: both figures (300-m body text and 289.894507 m Appendix A spatialResolution attribute) are in the same release-notes document, verified present as stated; the Appendix A value describes the L3-binned Integerized Sinusoidal grid rather than the mapped GeoTIFF.

Confirmed: the UMM-C DOI object gives 10.5067/MERGED-S3/OLCI/L3M/CYAN/CI/6.0 (the distributed, catalogued collection DOI); the release notes' Appendix A NetCDF global attribute gives :doi = "10.5067/MERGED-S3/OLCI/L3B/CYAN/CI/6T" (the upstream L3-binned file's internal DOI string). Both quotes verified present as stated; as the researcher notes, this is not necessarily a real-world conflict since the two DOIs describe different products in the processing chain.

Confirmed: release notes say reprocessing will occur 'every 10 to 16 months' (src-release-notes-v6); the EPA page (updated June 9, 2026) says the data 'will continue to be made publicly available and reprocessed annually' (src-epa-cyan). Both quotes verified present as stated; genuine unresolved conflict between the NASA producer's own schedule language and EPA's paraphrase.

additional_findings: A discrepancy the researcher did not list: the V6 release notes (including the August 2025 known-issues update) still describe CyAN as formed by 'Four U.S. federal agencies - EPA, NASA, NOAA, and USGS' with no mention of USACE anywhere in the document, while the EPA CyAN page (updated June 9, 2026) states USACE joined the collaboration 'as of 2023'. NASA's own release-notes document has not been updated to reflect the fifth agency even though EPA's page has.

cl-cyan-format-granule-size: the granule JSON confirms the raw number 0.1351547241210938 for granule_size, but the fetched JSON itself never states a unit; 'MB' is CMR's well-documented standard unit for this field but is not literally present in the cited source. Left as confirmed because the number is unambiguous and undisputed, but flagged here since the unit is not directly sourced from the fetched JSON.

PDF-to-text extraction of the release notes inconsistently renders typographic punctuation: most instances of en-dashes (e.g. 'Four U.S. federal agencies – EPA...') and the ≥ sign (Known Issues item 5) are preserved as the true Unicode character, but three apostrophe/quote instances (NASA's / “AK”/“CONUS”) were transcribed into the claims file using straight ASCII marks instead of the source's curly Unicode marks -- these are the three 'corrected' claims above.

No claim's quoted text spans a '===== PAGE n =====' marker in the release-notes .txt file; every release-notes claim's quote falls entirely within one page's text block. The only hyphen-line-wrap breaks found in the whole document ('top-level', 'ground-truth', 'color-separated') are genuine hyphenated compound words at natural line-wrap points, not mid-word hyphenation artifacts, and none of them fall inside any claim's quoted span.

The three shapefile/tool href claims (MERIS_OLCI_Lakes.zip, CONUS_tiles_shapefile.zip, and the CyAN File Search 'Launch' link) were independently verified against the raw HTML anchor href attributes and match the URLs stated in each claim's value exactly.
limitations: Verification relied on a single fresh crawl on 2026-09-22; NASA Earthdata and EPA pages are dynamic and could change wording, and the CMR granule query returns the single newest granule at fetch time, so the specific granule id/size/date in the granule-based claims will drift as the archive grows.

No data files (.tif/.zip) were downloaded, per instructions; claims about shapefile contents (e.g. whether COMID is an attribute field) and pixel-level file structure could not be verified beyond what the HTML/JSON pages state.

For the four 'corrected' checks, the correction is limited to the quote's transcription (Unicode punctuation, or citing the href field instead of an adjacent JSON field); none of the four required a change to the claim's value or note text.
